description: Many cultures had a penchant for using massed archers in battle or an affinity for the bow. In ancient Persia and India, archery held an important place in both warfare and elite martial culture. The Achaemenid Persians fielded large numbers of skilled archers, often combining massed bow fire with spearmen and cavalry, while Persian nobles and mounted troops also practiced archery as a mark of military training and status. In ancient India, powerful longbows and composite bows were used by infantry, chariot crews, and cavalry, and archery featured prominently in both battlefield tactics and heroic literature. In both regions, the bow was valued for its range, versatility, and ability to support more heavily armed troops before close combat.
